label: static
text: locked-off static frame
note: Begins from stillness only. After a moving shot this reads as a hard stop unless the link is a cut.

label: push in
text: slow push in toward the subject
note: On a dolly the camera body moves; distinguish from zoom, which does not.

label: pull back
text: steady pull back, revealing what surrounds the subject

label: truck left
text: trucking left at a constant rate

label: truck right
text: trucking right at a constant rate

label: pan left
text: panning left from a fixed position
note: A pan is rotation from a fixed head; a truck is translation. Models frequently conflate them.

label: pan right
text: panning right from a fixed position

label: tilt up
text: tilting up from the subject

label: tilt down
text: tilting down onto the subject

label: orbit
text: orbiting the subject at a constant radius
note: Cannot begin from stillness across a carry — an orbit that starts mid-clip reads as a jolt.

label: roll
text: rolling about the lens axis
note: Distinct from a dutch angle, which is a fixed roll. Not in the closed set at SHOT-GRAMMAR §V.

label: crane up
text: craning up and away

label: crane down
text: craning down toward the subject

label: pedestal up
text: raising the camera vertically on the column
note: A pedestal raises the camera without the arc a crane describes. Hard to distinguish in a short clip.

label: pedestal down
text: lowering the camera vertically on the column

label: handheld follow
text: handheld, following the subject, small constant correction

label: steadicam
text: stabilised walking move, floating
note: Reads as a smooth translate at this length; the distinguishing float needs more frames than the envelope has.

label: tracking follow
text: travelling with the subject at their pace

label: rack focus
text: static frame, focus racking between two planes
note: The frame is locked; only focus moves. Treated as still on both sides.

label: zoom in
text: focal length increasing, camera stationary
note: Not in the closed set at SHOT-GRAMMAR §V. A zoom is an optical change, not a move; models render it as a push.

label: zoom out
text: focal length decreasing, camera stationary

label: dolly zoom
text: dolly and counter-zoom, subject scale held
note: Two simultaneous moves. SHOT-GRAMMAR §IV: one move per clip.

label: whip pan
text: rapid pan smearing the frame
note: Dropped at SHOT-GRAMMAR §V — needs more frames than the envelope has, and poisons the anchor frame.

label: corkscrew
text: orbiting while rising
note: Two moves wearing one name. Dropped at SHOT-GRAMMAR §V.

label: bullet-time orbit
text: full 360 orbit with time suspended
note: Needs far more frames than 97. Dropped at SHOT-GRAMMAR §V.
